links.targetTitle: Grove takes accounting ownership of the Peg Stability Module

title: An unpaid settlement owed to Grove counts toward its Total Risk Capital until Sky pays it
content:
A.2.8.2.10.2.2 records that Grove is owed 2,528,000 USDS from the true-up of prior Monthly Settlement Cycles, and adds a non-obvious treatment: "[u]ntil this amount is paid to Grove through the next Monthly Settlement Cycle, this credit counts toward Grove's Total Risk Capital (TRC)."

Total Risk Capital is the buffer Sky requires an Agent to hold against losses it might cause. Counting an unpaid receivable toward it means the debt Sky owes Grove functions, while outstanding, as capital standing behind Grove's risk exposure. Economically this is defensible — Sky can withhold the payable to absorb a loss, so it is genuinely loss-absorbing from Sky's perspective.

But it produces a counterintuitive dynamic: **settling the debt reduces Grove's TRC**. A payment that improves the counterparty's liquidity worsens its measured capital adequacy, so the act of paying may itself create a shortfall that must be covered another way.

It also means the credit is doing double duty — Grove has an earned claim on it *and* Sky is relying on it as a buffer. Both readings cannot survive an actual loss event, which is exactly when the question would be tested.
description: The 2,528,000 USDS true-up credit is treated as risk-bearing capital while outstanding, so Sky's payable doubles as the counterparty's capital buffer and paying it reduces that buffer.
